confidence_notes: I used five web searches. The food and drink figures mostly come from crowd-sourced aggregators. TravelTables' Kenting page (last updated July 2023) gives about USD 4.29 for an inexpensive meal, 26.80 for a mid-range meal for two, 2.14 for a 0.5 L domestic draft beer and 3.70 for a cappuccino. A Nomad Watch page with no date gives coffee at about 3.59, beer at about 3.13 and a meal at about 4.69. For Pingtung City, aggregators give a meal at about 4.7–5.0, a cappuccino at about 2.8–2.9 and a domestic beer at about 1.6–1.7. I raised these figures to allow for inflation since the data was collected, Kenting's tourist-strip and resort pricing, and July being peak beach season. Cocktail figures are less certain. They are based on one undated blog that put cocktails at a Hengchun bar at about NT$200, Taiwan bar guides giving NT$150–250 for budget cocktails and NT$350–500 for Taipei mid-tier bars, and the usual local ratio of roughly 2–2.5 times the price of a beer. Wine by the glass is similarly uncertain: Taipei hotel menus list NT$320–420, so I scaled down to a typical Kenting restaurant. My working rate was about TWD 31 per USD. Accommodation figures come from general knowledge only, not booking searches. They assume July peak-season rates, when Kenting minsu and hotels often charge well above off-season prices, so they are the least certain anchors. The RBA rate of 0.6720 USD per AUD is the 4.00 pm figure for 18 November 2026, found through a search that surfaced the RBA exchange-rate feed. I couldn't confirm a 19 November figure.
comparable_city_reasoning: I started from Pingtung City and Hengchun (the township that contains Kenting) aggregator prices, plus older TravelTables and Nomad Watch figures for Kenting itself. I then raised them to reflect a seasonal beach-resort market, roughly similar to Taitung or Hualien tourist areas but with steeper peak-summer accommodation premiums. Taipei bar and hotel-menu prices served as an upper bound for drinks.
